holidays.name: International Sloth Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to celebrating the world's slowest mammals. Fans honor sloths by lounging, napping, and moving at a leisurely pace, all while learning about the threats these tree-dwellers face in the wild.
holidays.origin: Created by AIAI, a sloth conservation organization in Colombia, to raise awareness about sloth conservation. It is observed on the third Saturday of October in many years, and October 20 is also widely used for sloth celebrations.
holidays.funFact: Sloths can take up to a month to digest a single leaf, and algae grow in their fur, giving them a greenish tint that helps camouflage them.

holidays.name: National Brandied Fruit Day
holidays.description: A boozy celebration of fruit preserved or soaked in brandy, from cherries to peaches. Enjoy them over ice cream, in cakes, or straight from the jar for a grown-up treat.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance that grew out of the old tradition of preserving fruit in spirits, which let people enjoy harvest flavors through the winter before refrigeration.
holidays.funFact: Some old-fashioned recipes called 'Rumtopf' keep a pot of fruit and alcohol going all season, adding new fruit as each one ripens.

holidays.name: National Day on Writing
holidays.description: A day when everyone is encouraged to put pen to paper, fingers to keyboard, or thumbs to phone, and celebrate the many ways we write, from grocery lists to epic poems.
holidays.origin: Established by the National Council of Teachers of English in 2009 and later recognized by the U.S. Senate, to highlight the importance of writing in everyday life.
holidays.funFact: The very first writing systems, such as Sumerian cuneiform, were originally used mostly for tracking grain and other goods, not for poetry or stories.

holidays.name: Command Z Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek celebration of the undo shortcut that has saved countless documents, designs, and embarrassing mistakes. Today is for appreciating second chances, at least on a computer.
holidays.origin: A playful internet observance on 10/20 referencing the keyboard shortcut for 'undo' used on Mac computers, popularized by tech and design communities online.
holidays.funFact: The undo function was reportedly first developed in the early 1970s for text editors, and Ctrl+Z and Command+Z have since become among the most-used shortcuts in computing.

holidays.name: National Mulligan Day
holidays.description: A day for forgiving yourself and others for mistakes and taking a do-over, inspired by the golf tradition of replaying a poor shot without penalty.
holidays.origin: Rooted in golf culture, where a mulligan is an informal free retry. The unofficial observance encourages applying that generosity to everyday life.
holidays.funFact: The origin of the word 'mulligan' is disputed, with one popular legend crediting a Canadian golfer named David Mulligan in the 1920s.
